tex_content.html:
Proposition

(Generalized Laplace expansion.) Let $M$ be a square matrix over $R$ whose rows and columns are indexed by the disjoint union $\iota _a \sqcup \iota _b$, and write $k = \# \iota _a$, $l = \# \iota _b$. Then \[ \sum _{\sigma \in S_{\iota _a \sqcup \iota _b}} \operatorname {sgn}(\sigma )\, \det \big(M[\iota _a, \sigma |_a]\big)\, \det \big(M[\iota _b, \sigma |_b]\big) = k!\, l!\, \det M, \] where $M[\iota _a, \sigma |_a]$ is the submatrix with rows the $\iota _a$-rows of $M$ and columns $\sigma (\iota _a)$-columns in the order induced by $\sigma $, and similarly for $\iota _b$.
Proof

Expand both minors by the Leibniz formula: the left-hand side becomes

\[ \sum _{\sigma } \sum _{\pi \in S_{\iota _a}} \sum _{\rho \in S_{\iota _b}} \operatorname {sgn}(\sigma )\operatorname {sgn}(\pi )\operatorname {sgn}(\rho ) \prod _{i \in \iota _a} M_{\pi (i)\, \sigma (i)} \prod _{j \in \iota _b} M_{\rho (j)\, \sigma (j)}, \]

indices read in $\iota _a \sqcup \iota _b$. Fix $(\pi , \rho )$ and substitute $\sigma = \tau \circ (\pi \oplus \rho )^{-1}$, i.e. reindex the outer sum by $\tau = \sigma \circ (\pi \oplus \rho )$, where $\pi \oplus \rho $ is the permutation of $\iota _a \sqcup \iota _b$ acting as $\pi $ on $\iota _a$ and $\rho $ on $\iota _b$. Reindexing the two products by $\pi $ and $\rho $ respectively turns them into $\prod _{i} M_{i\, \tau (i)} \prod _{j} M_{j\, \tau (j)} = \prod _{x \in \iota _a \sqcup \iota _b} M_{x\, \tau (x)}$, and the signs combine as $\operatorname {sgn}(\tau )\operatorname {sgn}(\pi )^2\operatorname {sgn}(\rho )^2 = \operatorname {sgn}(\tau )$. The inner sum is therefore the Leibniz expansion of $\det M^{T} = \det M$, independent of $(\pi , \rho )$, and there are $k!\, l!$ such pairs.

□

Two further counting lemmas concern permutations of a disjoint union $\iota _a \sqcup \iota _b$ with $\# \iota _a = k$ and $\# \iota _b = l$; they drive the collapse of the permutation sums in the characterization of the Hodge star operator in equation prop:hodge-star-operator. We say a permutation $\chi $ of $\iota _a \sqcup \iota _b$ preserves the blocks if it maps the $\iota _a$-summand into itself, or equivalently the $\iota _b$-summand into itself; the block-preserving permutations are exactly those of the form $\pi \oplus \rho $ with $(\pi , \rho ) \in S_{\iota _a} \times S_{\iota _b}$.
